title: Scrap Kings - full-AI mobile game launch experiment
author: shadow_nik21
selftext:
Hey guys! Wanted to share some of our experience with developing mobile games with AI. Quick disclaimer: this is self-promo and there are store links below - but the main part of the post are the workflows we built (art pipeline + ad creatives) as required by the rules of this community.

**The game**

Scrap Kings is pretty simple. You collect scrap, buy units that defend your base from waves of the enemies, then you attack your opponent's base. There are some rogue-like elements baked into it with improvements to your base and cars in and outside runs. There are a lot of cars with their own mechanics (monster truck that climbs its target, wrecking ball on a chain, medic van...), bosses and arenas. Components-wise game has in-app purchases, rewarded ads (Approving mediation), analytics & attribution connected (Singular to track Unity and Google Ads US campaigns). 

And all of it is done with Claude. 100%

[Google Play](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.hostailegames.scrapkings) | [Play in browser, no install](https://difsyed0suunb.cloudfront.net/scrapkings/) | iOS is in TestFlight, coming soon.

It took \~3 weeks from the first prompt to Google Play prod release.

**What "100% Claude" means**

* Code: all of it. \~11k lines of TypeScript (one canvas, no game engine), \~4k lines of tests and \~12k lines of tooling.
* Art: all of it, and NO image models. Claude writes generators (see below)
* Music: 2 loops synthesized in numpy. Sound effects + 1 ad track: ElevenLabs through MCP, driven by Claude (the whole SFX pack cost $0.17 in credits).
* Ads: creatives (videos and banners), playables - all rendered from the game itself by Claude and created tools
* Manipulating all the platforms: Claude Cowork with browser extension. We already had all the accounts set-up everywhere from our previous projects, so it was mostly filling-in all these fields for new project, creating new UA campaigns and etc. 
* People involvement: briefs, reviews, tests, balance numbers, final "publish" buttons across platforms.

**Workflow 1: art without an image model**

We needed cars x damage states x driving/attack animations in ONE consistent style, and we change our mind about the style a LOT. So instead of drawing, Claude writes a generator:

1. A car is a Python "design" (a list of parts: body, cab, saw, boom...) + a rig with animation keys.
2. The generator turns panels into mismatched bolted plates, poses every frame and draws 4 damage states (damage = plates falling off).
3. SVG atlas → headless Chrome → webp sprite sheet + JSON. One command regenerates ALL art and it's deterministic.

Three things that made it work:

* [CLAUDE.md](http://CLAUDE.md) rule and hooks: "Never hand-author assets. Change the generator, regenerate, LOOK at the result, commit."
* Options first: for a new look Claude renders 3-4 options inside the REAL game screen, we pick, then we refine. We went through 20+ style explorations and rejected most of them.
* Verify by looking: Claude takes headless screenshots and contact sheets of the real game and actually looks at them before saying "done".

Audio: Claude can't obviously hear what was generated by Eleven labs same way it can "look" at images, so it picks takes by spectrogram and loudness numbers, and we made the final call by ear on a "sound board" page it generated (keep / redo + note per sound). 40 sounds decided in one session.

**Workflow 2: ad creatives straight from the game**

No creative is drawn by hand. The game has dev hooks that stage any scene deterministically (seeded RNG, frame-by-frame stepping), so Claude basically "films" the real game:

* Promo video (31 sec, vertical): 22 shots on a 140 BPM grid so every cut lands on the beat, the game's own music and its own sound effects replayed from a sound log. `npm run video` re-renders it in \~70 sec after any change to the game
* 3 playable ads: single-file HTML (3.4 MB, MRAID 3.0) built from the real game code. 12 headless smoke runs check network requests, errors and the store button before upload. 
* 35 static banners (20 Google App images, 12 Google display, 3 Unity end cards). Claude researched the specs itself and found things we would've missed. Every banner passes "gates" before it's saved: exact size, byte cap (display <= 150 KB), no Download/Install words, never upscaled, and every caption must be listed in a file with a line on why it's true in the game (no fake promises in ads)

**The UA part**

Claude drives the dashboards (Unity Ads, Google Ads, Singular for attribution) through browser control: creates campaigns, uploads creative packs, reads the stats and decides what to change next. We only keep the budget and the go-live click.

**TLDR (our experience, may not be applicable to you):**

* [CLAUDE.md](http://CLAUDE.md) and hooks are THE CONTRACT: never deploy / spend / publish without an explicit go for THAT action, never read env files, don't guess numbers (run a probe), and the human sets the game balance, Claude only reports
* Claude write docs for Claude: a decision log (\~12k lines of docs) + 10 project "skills" (video, banners, playtest, assets, deploy...) let a fresh session continue where the last one stopped
* Gates beat promises: one command (tsc + lint + unit tests + e2e) before every push, and every found bug becomes a lint rule or a test.
* Make everything change-related a / command. For example - when the game or the art changes - ads need to be re-rendered. We have special / commands for that where you basically just tell it how you want it changed and it runs whole re-gen / re-rendering process itself

P.S. This post was mostly written by Claude (but significantly less than the game itself!)
